headline: Construction to begin on Australia's largest wind farm in two years
facts: Danish investors Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners acquired the Gawara Baya wind farm project from WindLab and announced that construction of 68 turbines and a 100-megawatt battery near Mount Fox in north Queensland will begin imminently. The project is the first wind farm to reach construction under the federal government's Capacity Investment Scheme, which guarantees electricity prices to reduce investor risk. Local resident group Keep Mount Fox Wild opposes the development over environmental and biodiversity concerns, while project developers and local council representatives cite economic benefits and employment creation of about 500 construction jobs.
titles: The residents and wind farm on the frontline of Australia's energy wars
The residents and wind farm on the frontline of Australia's energy wars

headline: Australia's child raising costs reach $17,800 annually as birth rates fall
facts: National advocacy group The Parenthood reported that the annual cost of raising one child in Australia is about $17,800, and more than $36,500 for raising two children. The Parenthood chief executive Georgie Dent stated that affordability is a major driver of Australia's falling birth rate. Australia's fertility rate fell from 2.02 in 2008 to 1.48 in 2024, and the intergenerational report projects it will decline to 1.34 by 2065-66. Research commissioned by The Parenthood found that 86 per cent of parents in regional, rural, and remote areas experience financial stress tied to childcare access.
titles: Australia's child costs hit $17,800 a year, pushing would-be parents to have fewer kids
Australia's child costs hit $17,800 a year, pushing would-be parents to have fewer kids

headline: Intergenerational Report projects higher superannuation balances and fewer pensioners by 2066
facts: The 2026 Intergenerational Report projects that the number of Australians aged 67 or over will rise from 4.7 million in 2024 to 9 million in 2066. The report estimates that the median superannuation balance for Australians aged 65 to 69 will increase from $204,000 in 2024 to $450,000 in 2066. Access to the federal age pension is projected to fall from 66 per cent of retirees today to 52 per cent by 2066, reducing pension spending from 2.3 per cent of GDP to 1.8 per cent.
titles: House poor, super rich: The one area young Australians are winning
House poor, super rich: The one area young Australians are winning

headline: Liquidators investigate $5m cash withdrawals from failed NDIS housing company
facts: Liquidators report that $5.28 million in cash was withdrawn in 10 separate transactions from company accounts of Fairy Meadow House Pty Ltd before it went into liquidation. The company, directed by Shaun Mowbray, raised approximately $10 million from about 60 investors to build Specialist Disability Accommodation in Wollongong, but nothing was built. Mr Mowbray was declared bankrupt in July with $150 in the bank, and liquidators intend to lodge a report with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission regarding potential criminal breaches.
titles: $5m cash withdrawn from NDIS housing company before it went bust
$5m cash withdrawn from NDIS housing company before it went bust

headline: Australian Defence Force tests autonomous Ghost Bat aircraft amid AI integration push
facts: The Australian-made autonomous aircraft known as the Ghost Bat successfully shot down a target with an air-to-air missile over South Australia in late December last year. Chief of Air Force Air Marshal Stephen Chappell stated that the Ghost Bat operates using deterministic programming based on thousands of pre-designed options rather than live AI decision-making, and requires final operator authorisation before launching weapons. The International Institute for Strategic Studies stated that Israel's use of AI in warfare has increased exponentially since October 7, while the United Nations and the International Committee of the Red Cross recently called for a ban on unpredictable autonomous weapons.
titles: Ghost Bats and Maven Smart: How AI is transforming Defence
Ghost Bats and Maven Smart: How AI is transforming Defence

headline: A lawyer breaks down legal myths and realities for young Australians
facts: Lawyer Guglielmo Plain outlined legal realities and common misconceptions for young Australians, including criminal records, parental phone surveillance, joint criminal enterprise, and social media laws. The minimum age of criminal responsibility varies by state, ranging from under 10 in New South Wales, Queensland, South Australia, Tasmania, Western Australia, and the Northern Territory, to under 12 in Victoria and under 14 in the Australian Capital Territory. The age of sexual consent is 17 in South Australia and Tasmania, and 16 in all other states and territories.
titles: We answer what young people want to know about the law
We answer what young people want to know about the law

headline: EV owner warns motorists to maintain battery charge during bushfire season
facts: An experienced electric vehicle driver, Nigel Raynard, encountered difficulties during January when his Tesla reached a bushfire evacuation zone near Boddington with less than 15 per cent battery charge and local power outages. EV FireSafe CEO Emma Sutcliffe stated that electric vehicles are no more likely to catch fire in a bushfire than petrol or diesel vehicles, though damaged lithium-ion batteries carry a post-incident fire risk. The Electric Vehicle Council reported that Australia has more than 684,000 electric vehicles and hybrids on the road, including over 504,000 fully electric vehicles as of the end of August.
titles: Warning from EV owner caught with low charge in bushfire
Warning from EV owner caught with low charge in bushfire

headline: Visa slowdown halts working holidaymaker arrivals and disrupts Australian au pair market
facts: The federal government paused processing working holidaymaker visas in July to finalize migration caps, leading to industry warnings of stranded travel plans for backpackers. Immigration Minister Tony Burke announced caps on backpackers staying longer than a year, enabling visa processing to resume. Cultural Au Pair Association of Australia secretary Jackie Rylance and International Au Pairs Association managing director Patricia Brunner stated that backlogs and delays are leaving Australian host families without childcare support.
titles: Families scramble to find childcare after visa slowdown hits au pairs

headline: Australia faces challenge to expand domestic mineral processing and supply chain
facts: The resources sector accounts for 60% of Australia’s export revenue, with 448 operating mines as of December 2025, according to the provided text. The Minerals Council of Australia (MCA) reports that developing a new mine can take up to 18 years for nickel and 15 years for copper, and the world will need 50 new lithium mines, 60 new nickel mines, and 17 new cobalt mines by 2030. Anax Metals is restarting the Whim Creek operation in Western Australia as a regional processing hub with a new concentrator forecast to produce 10,000 to 12,000 tonnes per annum of copper-equivalent.
titles: Australia’s mining powerhouse facing its next test: A world tour

headline: Gold Coast council aims to move past tourism cliché to build broader economy
facts: The Gold Coast City Council's marketing organisation, Brand Gold Coast, is working to reinvent the city's reputation beyond a laid-back beach lifestyle and tourism focus to attract serious business, study and investment. Brand Gold Coast marketing boss Todd Babiak stated that the city's film industry currently has a gross value of $420 million and has produced international blockbusters including Thor, Aquaman and Elvis. Documentary producer Chris Amos stated that overseas productions come to the Gold Coast for financial benefits but intellectual property rights go offshore.
titles: The Gold Coast is done with being 'the Glitter Strip', so what's next?

headline: Australian homebuyers face borrowing power cuts and suburb lockouts from rate rises
facts: An analysis by REA Group shows that a single interest rate cut or hike impacts household borrowing capacities, reducing the national average homebuying household's capacity from $877,000 down to $858,000, with a second hike reducing it to $840,000. Australian Bureau of Statistics figures show the typical home loan in June was $731,000, requiring a minimum household income of about $162,500 per year. Real Estate Institute of Australia president Jacob Caine stated that 59 per cent of the median family income is currently spent on mortgage repayments, exceeding $6,000 a month.
titles: 101 Australian suburbs average homebuyer will lose after rate rise

headline: WA Severe Thunderstorm Warning Issued for Heavy Rain
facts: The Bureau of Meteorology issued a severe thunderstorm warning for the South Coastal, South West, and South East Coastal districts on Sunday, 27 September 2026. Heavy rain and thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding in locations including Albany, Bremer Bay, Walpole, and Denmark. A 90km/h wind gust was recorded at Wiluna Airport at 2:17pm. The Department of Fire and Emergency Services advised residents to stay indoors, avoid specific hazards, and take precautions against potential flooding and fallen power lines.
titles: WA Severe Thunderstorm Warning: Heavy Rain

headline: Subiaco to Scrap Physical Parking Machines at Nine Locations
facts: The City of Subiaco is removing cash payment machines at nine parking locations as part of a parking system overhaul running from September to mid-to-late December. Motorists at these locations will be required to use a smartphone via a secure payment web page or the EasyPark app to pay for parking. Physical machines will remain available at other locations, including six machines accepting cash across five locations on Barker Road, Hensman Road, Park Street, and Railway Road. Parking fees and weekend and weekday after-5pm free parking rules will not change.
titles: Major changes coming to parking payments in a western suburb

headline: West Australian Indian Film Council launched to connect Perth and Mumbai
facts: The West Australian Indian Film Council (WAIFC) was formally launched at Government House in Perth on 11 September 2026. Founded and chaired by Nilesh Makwana, the council aims to link universities, screen professionals, businesses, and cultural organisations in Western Australia and Mumbai. The initiative highlights Western Australia's filming locations, Perth Film Studios' four soundstages, and Screenwest's production attraction incentives.
titles: Perth’s cinematic promise meets Mumbai’s creative energy

headline: Bond market sell-off points to rising inflation and economic risks
facts: Global bond markets have experienced a severe sell-off as investors demand higher yields amid rising inflation and economic risks. The US 10-year and 30-year government bond yields are near two-decade highs, driven by stronger-than-expected US manufacturing data showing input prices growing at their fastest pace in four years. Germany expects federal borrowing to reach a record 525.5 billion euros in 2026, while Japan's 10-year bond yield reached its highest level since 1996.

headline: ACT Treasurer warns GST carve-up threatens egalitarian values
facts: ACT Treasurer Chris Steel told the Productivity Commission that current GST revenue distribution arrangements risk entrenching inequality and cost the territory 900 school teachers' salaries without the no-worse-off guarantee. Mr Steel called for a return to the pre-2018 GST distribution method, ending population share floors and temporary top-up payments. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese stated the GST deal would not change, while the Western Australian government dismissed the Productivity Commission's report as the work of 'east coast clowns'.
titles: Fix the GST carve-up or Australia's egalitarian values are at risk: Steel

headline: Brisbane teenager in critical condition after hit-and-run crash
facts: A 16-year-old boy from Wynnum is in a critical, life-threatening condition at Princess Alexandra Hospital after being struck by two vehicles on Old Cleveland Road in Belmont. Emergency services attended the scene at about 9.45pm on Saturday. The first vehicle, described as a dark SUV, fled the scene before police arrived, while the second vehicle remained with its 19-year-old driver uninjured.
titles: Brisbane teenager in critical condition after being struck by two cars

headline: Severe storms and cold fronts grip southern and western Australia
facts: Sydney faces a wet and windy Sunday with a 95 per cent chance of rain and a forecast high of 18C, while Melbourne expects a high of 17C after starting at 9C. Western Australia faces severe thunderstorms extending across the Goldfields and moving southeast, with Perth reaching a high of 22C with a 70 per cent chance of rain. Fire bans remain in place across parts of Queensland's central outback, with fires northwest of Bundaberg uncontrolled, and Tasmania is under a frost warning after snow fell to about 600 metres.
titles: Chilly Sunday ahead for southeast as storms and fire danger grip parts of Australia

facts: Former Trivett luxury car dealership owner Greg Duncan and his wife Glenda sold their Bellevue Hill home via private treaty for about $31 million on September 22. The Duncans originally purchased the four-bedroom, four-bathroom house for $1.45 million in 1996. NRL player Nathan Cleary purchased a Curl Curl house for $5.5 million in June from Stewart House.

headline: Iran insists on diplomacy after US rejects peace proposal
facts: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that only diplomacy and a negotiated solution could resolve the conflict with the United States and Israel. US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian peace proposal that was transmitted via Qatari mediators to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and pause regional fighting. Trump claimed Iran pushed for a deal because it was losing the conflict, while Araghchi said Iran is waiting for mediators to convey definitive views before deciding its next steps.
titles: Iran insists on diplomatic solution after Trump rejects peace plan
Trump rejects Iran peace proposal

headline: Pope Leo draws massive crowds for outdoor Mass in Paris
facts: An estimated 800,000 people attended an outdoor Mass celebrated by Pope Leo along the Champs-Elysees in Paris during his four-day tour of France. The Pope urged Catholics to find happiness in faith rather than materialism and warned against the unchecked development of artificial intelligence during a speech at UNESCO. Pope Leo is scheduled to visit Lourdes to meet with seven French victims of church abuse.
titles: Hundreds of thousands in Paris cheer Pope Leo in largest event of French tour

headline: Former beauty queen turned anti-coup fighter shares Myanmar story in film
facts: Htar Htet Htet, a Myanmar actor, businesswoman and 2013 Miss Grand International contestant, joined anti-coup protests and later resistance fighters in the jungle following the February 2021 military coup. She has starred in a new film titled Ray, which she describes as a 95 per cent accurate account of her experiences during Myanmar's slide into civil war. Htar Htet Htet now lives in Australia, where she works as a gymnastics coach two days a week in Sydney.
titles: Meet the beauty queen turned freedom fighter who made her home in Australia

headline: Rovos Rail operates 15-day Copper Trail luxury journey across Africa
facts: Rovos Rail runs a 15-day Copper Trail luxury train itinerary spanning 3,100 kilometres from Victoria Falls in Zimbabwe through Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, terminating at Lobito in Angola. The journey carries 57 passengers aboard the Pride of Africa. The route traverses the Lobito Corridor, which includes sections supported by Chinese and European funding alongside segments requiring infrastructure repair.
titles: This 3100-km adventure is one of the world’s great rail journeys

headline: Washington court pauses state fines against ranchers in wetlands dispute
facts: A Washington appellate court commissioner ruled that the state Pollution Control Hearings Board cannot continue its fight to fine Wade and Teresa King while they seek a jury trial. The Washington Department of Ecology alleges the King family illegally excavated 23 areas within protected wetlands, issuing a quarter-million-dollar fine and threatening potential criminal charges. The Pacific Legal Foundation argues that subjecting individuals to administrative penalties without an independent jury trial is unconstitutional.
titles: Court stalls Washington from being ‘judge and prosecutor’ in fight against ranchers

headline: Kalonzo Musyoka accuses President Ruto of planning to influence the 2027 General Election
facts: Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka accused President William Ruto's administration of planning to influence the 2027 General Election by mobilising voters from Uganda. Speaking at a rally in Busia County on Saturday, Kalonzo alleged that individuals from Uganda would be given Kenyan identity cards to vote for President Ruto. Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen led a Kenya Kwanza delegation to Bukwo District in Uganda on Friday for a cross-border political meeting addressing security and the movement of citizens.
titles: 'Ata ukiongeza kura Uganda, wewe ni one term!' Kalonzo slams Ruto over Murkomen’s border mobilisation

headline: U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal Condemns Trump’s Pocket Rescissions
facts: U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal released a statement condemning Trump’s pocket rescissions, stating they are illegal and target immigration services. She stated that the rescissions cut essential services for immigrants, including assistance for unaccompanied children, legal services for citizenship, integration efforts, and education programs. Jayapal stated that Congress has the constitutional authority to appropriate funding under Article 1 and vowed to prevent the rescissions.
titles: Ranking Member Jayapal Statement on Trump’s Pocket Rescissions

facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia increased the cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.6 per cent, reaching a 15-year high. Australia's annual headline inflation rate rose to 4 per cent for the 12 months to August 2026, driven by a 14.8 per cent spike in fuel prices. Economists note that larger average home loans and higher household debt levels compared to 2011 mean rate rises have a more severe impact on mortgage holders.

facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia lifted the official cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60%. Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, National Australia Bank and ANZ announced they will pass the full 0.25 percentage point increase onto variable home loan customers from 9 October. Commonwealth Bank also confirmed eligible variable-rate business loans will rise by 0.25 percentage points from the same date.

headline: Specialist crews remove 31-tonne whale carcass from City Beach
facts: Specialist contractors using heavy machinery, an excavator and a truck began removing a 13-metre, 31-tonne humpback whale carcass from South City Beach on Wednesday. The Town of Cambridge estimated the removal and landfill disposal costs at between $60,000 and $100,000. The presence of the carcass drew large crowds and attracted several great white sharks close to shore, prompting a beach closure, exclusion zones and $250 fines for unauthorized access.

headline: Kondinin Wind Farm Reaches Financial Close for 130MW Stage 1
facts: Foresight Group reached financial close on the 130MW first stage of the Kondinin Wind Farm in Western Australia's Wheatbelt, securing A$430 million in debt financing to begin construction. Foresight acquired full ownership of the broader 370MW project after buying out Shell Energy's 50% stake. Stage 1 will use 21 Vestas turbines, is backed by a 7-year Power Purchase Agreement with Synergy and a 15-year Australian Government Capacity Investment Scheme agreement, and is designated as a Priority Project under the State Development Act.
titles: Foresight closes financing on 130MW Kondinin wind farm in Western Australia

headline: Great white sharks circle Swanbourne beach after whale carcass washes ashore
facts: Surf Life Saving WA reported a whale carcass washed ashore near Swanbourne in Perth on Monday morning. The Surf Life Saving helicopter spotted three four-metre great white sharks circling about 15 metres from the shore at approximately 2.45pm, alongside a hammerhead and two tiger sharks in nearby waters. City Beach was closed one kilometre north and south of the location as a precaution while authorities manage the carcass.

headline: Whale Carcass at City Beach Prompts Closures and Shark Sightings
facts: A whale carcass washed up at City Beach on Monday, drawing several sharks including two great whites measuring 5 metres and 4 metres just 10 metres from the shore. The Town of Cambridge closed local beaches for three days and prepared for a removal operation estimated to cost between 40,000 and 60,000 Australian dollars. Fisheries Minister Jackie Jarvis stated that towing the carcass out to sea was avoided due to the risk of it breaking up and washing back ashore.

headline: WA Government considers Bullsbrook quarantine centre for prison use
facts: Western Australia's Corrective Services Commissioner Brad Royce and Corrective Services Minister Tony Buti stated on Wednesday that the $400 million Commonwealth-owned Bullsbrook quarantine centre remains under consideration for conversion into a prison if it becomes available. A feasibility study began in June, driven by overcrowding and a prison population strain that led to a "show cause" notice for Hakea, Casuarina and Melaleuca prisons. Simultaneously, the state announced a $100 million court security arrangement employing 127 full-time staff under the Sheriff's Office to free up 45,000 police hours.

headline: JCDecaux Launches Nurture for Country Campaign with Chalkwest
facts: JCDecaux launched its Nurture for Country program with its first partner, Chalkwest, an Aboriginal-owned vehicle rental provider in Western Australia. The campaign aims to elevate First Nations businesses through Out-of-Home advertising, starting with a phase delivered in collaboration with Perth Airport before rolling out across the state. Chalkwest is led by Managing Director Zak Kirkup and operates a fleet of more than 1,300 vehicles across 12 towns and seven airports.

headline: Australia bans card payment surcharges starting October
facts: New payment scheme rules following an RBA review take effect to end payment surcharges for EFTPOS, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, and PayPal. Payment networks have integrated bans into merchant contracts, and terminal software will be updated automatically to disable surcharge features. Standard weekend hospitality surcharges, public holiday fees, and ticketing booking fees remain legal if applied independently of payment method, while RBA consumer credit card interchange fee caps drop from 0.80 per cent to 0.30 per cent.

headline: August inflation jumps to 4 per cent as rate hike fears grow
facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported headline inflation jumped to 4.0 per cent in the year to August, up from 3.5 per cent in July. Automotive fuel prices surged 15 per cent following Middle East conflict and the end of fuel excise relief, while new dwelling prices rose 5.4 per cent over 12 months. Underlying trimmed mean inflation remained steady at 3.6 per cent.

headline: Reserve Bank of Australia raises cash rate to 4.60 per cent
facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board voted unanimously to raise the official cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.60 per cent, taking effect on September 30, 2026. The RBA cited headline inflation climbing to 4.0 per cent in August and persistent capacity constraints as drivers for the fourth rate hike of the year. Underlying trimmed mean inflation remained at 3.6 per cent, and the unemployment rate stood at 4.6 per cent.
titles: Reserve Bank of Australia Raises Cash Rate to 4.60 Percent as August Inflation Rebounds to 4.0 Percent

headline: WA Government provides up to $4 million to restart Cardup brickworks
facts: The Western Australian Government is providing up to $4 million to support the recommissioning of the mothballed Austral brickworks in Cardup. The facility is expected to produce approximately 17 million Maxibricks and increase state brick production by 10 to 15 per cent once operational. The funding package includes a $3 million upfront contribution for maintenance, a $500,000 incentive to resume operations by March 2027, and a $500,000 incentive for delivering 17 million bricks within 12 months.

headline: News Australia and CommBank launch national housing affordability campaign
facts: News Australia and CommBank launched a national campaign named 'The Home Front' on Monday across news.com.au and State & Community mastheads. The campaign is informed by the National Housing Affordability Project research conducted in July by The Growth Distillery and SEC Newgate Research surveying 2,048 Australians aged 18 and over. The survey found that 53 per cent of non-homeowners want to buy a first home but only 14 per cent believe it will happen soon, 51 per cent of aspiring first-home buyers have surrendered hope, and 68 per cent of renters believe they will rent for life.

headline: Greens leader Larissa Waters steps down due to health reasons
facts: Australian Greens Leader Larissa Waters announced she is stepping down from the party leadership due to a downturn in her pre-existing kidney disease. Senator Waters said the demands of leadership and travel are incompatible with her recovery, though her prognosis is positive. She will remain in parliament as a Senator for Queensland and take a period of medical leave. A party room meeting will be held later this week to elect a new leader.

headline: Australian household spending unchanged in August as transport offsets falls
facts: Australian household spending was unchanged in seasonally adjusted terms in August, following increases of 1.1 per cent in July and 0.9 per cent in June, according to Australian Bureau of Statistics data. ABS head of business statistics Tom Lay reported that recreation and culture spending saw the largest fall at 1.4 per cent, alongside declines in clothing and footwear, recreational goods, food, health, and furniture. These falls were offset by a 2.3 per cent increase in transport spending driven by an 8.1 per cent rise in fuel spending following the full restoration of fuel excise duty on August 3.

headline: Victorian doctors stage mass walkout over pay and working conditions
facts: Thousands of doctors from major Victorian hospitals will walk off the job on Thursday afternoon for a four-hour strike. The action follows over 14 months of negotiations with the Victorian government. Doctors are calling for a 30 per cent pay rise over four years, a 12.5-hour shift cap, paid overtime, and three consecutive days off per fortnight.

headline: RBA says home price plunge poses no major stability risk
facts: The Reserve Bank of Australia stated in its half-yearly Financial Stability Review that less than one per cent of borrowers are estimated to be facing negative equity. RBA modelling suggests that housing prices could fall by 20 per cent from current levels and only about five per cent of mortgages would enter negative equity. The report follows the RBA lifting interest rates by 25 basis points to 4.6 per cent on Tuesday, while headline inflation rose to 4.0 per cent.

headline: Ampol buys Evie Networks for $225 million
facts: Fuel giant Ampol agreed to acquire 100 per cent of Evie Networks for $225 million, adding more than 1,000 charging bays to its existing network. The combined platform will feature 1,425 charging bays across more than 400 sites, with the transaction expected to complete in the first half of 2027 subject to ACCC clearance. Ampol reported that charging sessions and energy volume on its AmpCharge network more than doubled in the first half of 2026.

headline: National dwelling approvals drop 6.1 per cent in August
facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that total dwelling approvals fell 6.1 per cent in August to 16,953. Private sector house approvals rose 3.7 per cent to 10,885 dwellings, marking eight consecutive months above 10,000. Private sector dwellings excluding houses fell 21.2 per cent to 5,674 dwellings, driven by declines in apartment and townhouse approvals.

headline: Australian Consumer Price Index Rises 4.0 Percent in Year to August 2026
facts: The Australian Bureau of Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 4.0 per cent in the 12 months to August 2026, up from 3.5 per cent in July. Housing was the largest contributor to annual inflation, increasing by 5.7 per cent due to higher costs for new dwellings and electricity. Transport was the second largest contributor, rising by 5.6 per cent driven by automotive fuel prices, which jumped 14.8 per cent in August.

facts: The Australian Greens party room elected David Shoebridge as its new leader in an 11-member ballot in Sydney, following the resignation of Larissa Waters due to ill health. Senator Shoebridge defeated Mehreen Faruqi seven votes to four after preferences, with Steph Hodgins-May elected as deputy leader. Senator Shoebridge stated that the party aims to replace the Labor Party and focus on the cost of living and corporate opposition.

facts: The Reserve Bank increased the cash rate to 4.6 per cent, marking a level not seen since October 2011 when the rate sat at 4.75 per cent. Cotality data shows that median house values have more than doubled since 2011 while wages have increased by about 49 per cent. The national dwelling value to income ratio has risen from 6.5 times to 8.7 times, and household debt has grown from 161 per cent to 178 per cent of disposable incomes.

facts: The Western Australian Government is investing more than $2 million into Geraldton Turf Club and Dongara Irwin Race Club. Geraldton Turf Club completed a $1.163 million irrigation system project and received $40,000 for rubber flooring in horse stalls, with further upgrades underway. facts: Kalgoorlie Super Pit workers Lance and Kristy Richards used the mine's daily explosives blast mixed with pink powder for a gender reveal. headline: Former Obstetrician Restores Western Australian Wheatbelt Property to Bushland
facts: Dr Susan Downes, a 76-year-old former GP obstetrician, has spent 11 years restoring a 200-hectare rural property north of York in Western Australia's wheatbelt. Aided by volunteers, she has planted approximately 45,000 trees across five planting seasons with a survival rate exceeding 40%. The property includes Mount Mackie, a site historically significant from Ensign Robert Dale's 1830 expedition and valued by local Indigenous communities.

headline: WA opposition criticises government over use of school transportable classrooms
facts: The WA opposition accused the state government of poor planning after a new parliamentary document revealed that over 4,000 transportable classrooms are currently in use across Western Australian schools, representing nearly one in six classrooms. Opposition education spokesman Liam Staltari stated that newer schools opened since 2017 are heavily reliant on demountables, with more than half of all classrooms at Wellard Primary School, Oakwood Primary School and Aspiri Primary School being transportable. Education Minister Sabine Winton defended the use of transportables as a cost-effective way to rapidly increase capacity, and stated that 11 new primary schools and two new high schools will be built between now and 2030 to address demand and remove transportables.

headline: Analysis Shows Australian Politicians Lead in AI Speech Usage
facts: An analysis by The Economist found that Australian politicians lead the English-speaking world in using artificial intelligence to write or assist with speeches. A random sample of parliamentary speeches between September 2025 and 2026 showed that more than 20 per cent of House of Representatives speeches and just under 15 per cent of Senate speeches were flagged by the Pangram AI content detector. Speaker Milton Dick stated there are no parliamentary rules governing the use of AI in speeches, though members remain responsible for their statements.

headline: Special WA Police powers take effect for Land Forces conference
facts: The Cook Labor Government's Land Forces (Special Powers) Act 2026 is in full effect from 1 to 10 October 2026. The legislation gives WA Police additional powers within designated security areas around the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre, where the Land Forces 2026 event runs from 6 to 8 October. Police Minister Reece Whitby stated the powers include establishing checkpoints, cordons, and roadblocks, searching people, bags, and vehicles, and issuing lawful directions, last used during the 2011 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

headline: Western Australia government provides $4 million bailout to restart Cardup brickworks
facts: The Western Australia government announced a support package of up to $4 million on September 29 to recommission the mothballed Austral brickworks at Cardup in south-eastern Perth. The package includes a $3 million upfront payment, a $500,000 incentive payment to resume production by March 2027, and $500,000 to deliver 17 million maxibricks within 12 months of opening. Housing Industry Association WA executive director Michael McGowan stated the support will boost state brick production by 10 to 15 per cent and support a broad cross-section of construction projects.

facts: Gay Bernadette Branchi, 88, was arrested and charged with attempted murder over allegations she tried to kill her husband, former Automotive Holdings Group chairman Robert Branchi. The accused was taken into custody from The Queenslea residential aged care home in Claremont where the couple shared a room. Following an initial court appearance via audio link and magistrate concerns regarding cognitive mental capacity and vulnerability, Mrs Branchi was granted bail.

facts: Tasmania Police took a man into custody and set up crime scenes at Burtonia Street in Rokeby and Holmfield Avenue in Clarendon Vale following a reported shooting on Wednesday at around 11:30am. Police stated a vehicle pulled up beside a walking pedestrian, and a single shot was fired in their direction before the vehicle left. No injuries were reported, the firearm and suspect vehicle were located, and Bellerive officers, the Special Operations Group and South East CIB are involved in the investigation.

headline: Dead humpback whale removed from Perth's City Beach
facts: A 72-tonne crane hired by the Town of Cambridge began lifting a 13-metre long, decomposing humpback whale carcass at about 10am at Perth's City Beach. The whale washed up on Monday and initially weighed 31 tonnes before being wrapped in a net and dragged 1.5 kilometres along the shore. Town of Cambridge Mayor Gary Mack stated the plan was to bury the whale in landfill and that the council planned to pay for the removal, while not ruling out asking the state government to foot the bill.

facts: Edith Cowan University (ECU) has joined the Additive Manufacturing Cooperative Research Centre (AMCRC) as its newest research partner. ECU will contribute to collaborative research programs, project development and workforce initiatives focused on additive manufacturing.

headline: US Court of International Trade hears challenge to Donald Trump's latest tariffs
facts: The US Court of International Trade heard arguments on Wednesday in a legal challenge brought by importers and 25 Democrat-led states against the Trump administration's 10 to 12.5 per cent tariffs imposed in late July on about 60 economies and 86 countries. The tariffs were implemented under Section 301 of the US Trade Act on the grounds that foreign failures to prevent imports of goods made with forced labour burdened US commerce. The challengers argued the tariffs are a pretext to recreate a global tariff regime previously ruled illegal by the courts and that the administration failed to follow required country-specific investigative processes.

headline: Sydney Metro to keep six platform doors closed on final M1 line section
facts: Sydney Metro has assured safety regulators it will keep six train and platform screen doors closed at stations along the final section of the $30 billion M1 metro line. Three screen doors will remain closed at Dulwich Hill station, and one each at Canterbury, Campsie and Marrickville, located at curved platforms where the distance between trains and platforms is widest. Transport Minister John Graham stated that 170 mechanical gap fillers have been installed across eight stations to ensure safe boarding.
